guide.title: A week in Austin
guide.author: Nate Bird
guide.summary: Seven days of brisket and breakfast tacos, live music every night, spring-fed swimming holes and bats over Lady Bird Lake.

places.name: The Driskill
places.notes: An 1886 cattle baron's hotel on Sixth Street, with a grand lobby bar.

places.name: Hotel San José
places.notes: A calm, minimalist bungalow court on South Congress, with a courtyard bar and pool.

places.name: Hotel Saint Cecilia
places.notes: The splurge. A Victorian house and poolside bungalows under old oaks, each with a turntable.

places.name: Austin Motel
places.notes: A bright, retro 1938 motel with a kidney-shaped pool. The fun, budget pick.

places.name: Franklin Barbecue
places.notes: The famous brisket. Queue early with a chair and a cooler, or preorder online weeks ahead.

places.name: la Barbecue
places.address: 2401 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78702
places.notes: Brisket that rivals Franklin's with a shorter line. Try the El Sancho sandwich.

places.name: Terry Black's Barbecue
places.notes: Cafeteria-style Texas barbecue with no preorder needed. Brisket, beef ribs and creamed corn.

places.name: Veracruz All Natural
places.notes: The migas taco, often called Austin's best breakfast taco.

places.name: Joe's Bakery & Coffee Shop
places.notes: A family-run Tex-Mex spot since 1962. Breakfast tacos and pan dulce.

places.name: Juan in a Million
places.address: 2300 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78702
places.notes: Home of the Don Juan, a breakfast taco so big it comes with spare tortillas.

places.name: Matt's El Rancho
places.notes: Classic Tex-Mex since 1952. Order the Bob Armstrong dip and a margarita.

places.name: Uchi
places.notes: Inventive Japanese in a converted bungalow. The happy hour is the best value.

places.name: Odd Duck
places.notes: Seasonal Texas small plates from a former food trailer. Share everything.

places.name: Kerbey Lane Cafe
places.notes: The original location of Austin's beloved all-day diner. Queso and gingerbread pancakes.

places.name: Jo's Coffee
places.notes: A walk-up coffee window next to the "i love you so much" mural.

places.name: Lick Honest Ice Creams
places.notes: Ice cream from Texas farms, in flavors like goat cheese with thyme and honey.

places.name: The Continental Club
places.notes: A 1955 music club with live bands every night. Monday and Tuesday regulars are a treat.

places.name: Broken Spoke
places.notes: A true Texas dance hall since 1964. Take the early two-step lesson, then dance.

places.name: The White Horse
places.notes: A honky-tonk with free dance lessons and live country every night.

places.name: Antone's Nightclub
places.notes: Austin's home of the blues since 1975, where Stevie Ray Vaughan cut his teeth.

places.name: Cosmic Coffee + Beer Garden
places.notes: Coffee, beer and food trucks in a big garden with chickens and a creek.

places.name: Texas State Capitol
places.notes: Taller than the U.S. Capitol, of course. Free tours, and stand in the middle of the rotunda to hear the echo.

places.name: Bullock Texas State History Museum
places.notes: The story of Texas, including a 17th-century French shipwreck raised from Matagorda Bay.

places.name: Blanton Museum of Art
places.address: 200 E Martin Luther King Jr Blvd, Austin, TX 78712
places.notes: A strong university museum, and Ellsworth Kelly's Austin, a chapel of colored light.

places.name: LBJ Presidential Library
places.notes: Civil rights, Vietnam and the Great Society, with an animatronic LBJ telling jokes.

places.name: Harry Ransom Center
places.notes: Free, with a Gutenberg Bible and the world's first photograph on show.

places.name: Ann W. Richards Congress Avenue Bridge
places.notes: A million and a half bats fly out at dusk from March to October. Watch from the bank or a boat.

places.name: Mexic-Arte Museum
places.notes: Mexican and Latino art downtown, with a beautiful Day of the Dead exhibition every fall.

places.name: Umlauf Sculpture Garden & Museum
places.notes: A shady sculpture garden by Zilker Park, with ponds and benches. Pair it with Barton Springs.

places.name: Elisabet Ney Museum
places.notes: A 19th-century sculptor's free castle-like studio in Hyde Park.

places.name: ACL Live at the Moody Theater
places.address: 310 W Willie Nelson Blvd, Austin, TX 78701
places.notes: Home of the Austin City Limits TV tapings, with the Willie Nelson statue out front.

places.name: Barton Springs Pool
places.notes: A three-acre spring-fed pool at 68 degrees all year. Bliss on a hot afternoon.

places.name: Zilker Metropolitan Park
places.notes: Austin's big backyard, with kayaks for rent on Barton Creek and the botanical garden nearby.

places.name: Ann and Roy Butler Hike-and-Bike Trail
places.address: Ann and Roy Butler Hike-and-Bike Trail, Austin, TX 78704
places.notes: Ten miles around Lady Bird Lake. Walk the boardwalk section for the skyline view.

places.name: Mount Bonnell
places.notes: A short climb to a view over the Colorado River and the 360 Bridge. Go at sunset.

places.name: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center
places.notes: Native Texas plants and wildflowers. Bluebonnet season is late March to April.

places.name: McKinney Falls State Park
places.notes: Limestone falls and swimming holes on Onion Creek, twenty minutes from downtown.

places.name: Hamilton Pool Preserve
places.address: 24300 Hamilton Pool Rd, Dripping Springs, TX 78620
places.notes: A collapsed grotto with a waterfall into a jade pool. Reservations are required; check before you go.
